t.7.29.1: Then, when darkness had arisen, the Rākṣasas, maddened by their strength, fought together with the gods, slaying one another.
t.7.29.3: But when that was enveloped in darkness, all those gods and Rākṣasas, fighting one another, could not recognize each other.
t.7.29.2: Then, by the army of the gods, only a tenth part of the great host of the rākṣasas was left standing in the battle; the rest was led to the abode of Yama.
t.7.29.4: Indra, Rāvaṇa, and the mighty Rāvaṇi, those three alone, did not fall into bewilderment in that battle shrouded by a web of darkness.
t.7.29.5: But Rāvaṇa, seeing his entire army slain in battle, fell into a fierce rage and let out a mighty roar.
t.7.29.6: In anger the unassailable one said to the charioteer standing in the chariot: "Drive me through the middle of the enemy army, all the way to its far end."
t.7.29.7: Today, in battle, I myself, with my feats of valour and with diverse weapons of great strength, shall destroy all these gods and drive them from the vault of the sky.
t.7.29.8: I shall slay Indra, Varuṇa, Dhanada and Yama; having swiftly struck down the thirty gods, I myself shall then stand above all.
t.7.29.9: Do not give way to despair; drive my chariot swiftly. Twice indeed I tell you today: carry me on to the very end.
t.7.29.10: This is that region of Nandana where we now are. Lead me today to the place where the Udaya mountain stands.
t.7.29.11: Hearing those words of his, the charioteer then directed the horses, swift as thought, right through the midst of the enemies.
t.7.29.12: Then Śakra, lord of the gods, standing in his chariot, having learned of that resolve of his, spoke these words to the gods who stood on the battlefield.
t.7.29.13: O gods, hear my words, this is what pleases me: let the Rākṣasa Daśagrīva be firmly seized while he is still alive.
t.7.29.15: This one cannot be slain today, for he is utterly fearless by virtue of the boon granted him. Therefore we shall capture this Rākṣasa; be vigilant in the battle!
t.7.29.14: For this exceedingly mighty one will charge into the army on his chariot, which has the force of the wind, like a towering wave in the ocean at the full moon.
t.7.29.16: Just as, having subdued Bali, I enjoy these three worlds, so too the subduing of this wicked one pleases me.
t.7.29.17: Then the greatly radiant Śakra, leaving Rāvaṇa and taking up a position elsewhere, fought on, destroying the Rākṣasas in battle.
t.7.29.18: Daśagrīva, unchecked, entered from the northern side, while Śatakratu entered by the southern flank.
t.7.29.19: Then the lord of the Rākṣasas, having penetrated a hundred yojanas, covered the entire army of the gods with showers of arrows.
t.7.29.20: Then Śakra, seeing that he had entered, calmly turned his own army back and surrounded Daśānana.
t.7.29.21: Meanwhile, seeing that Rāvaṇa seized by Śakra, the Dānavas and Rākṣasas let out a cry: "Alas, we are slain!"
t.7.29.22: Then Rāvaṇi, overwhelmed with rage, mounted his chariot and, exceedingly furious, entered that most dreadful army.
t.7.29.23: Entering that magic illusion given to him long ago by Gopati, he became invisible to all beings and showered that army with missiles.
t.7.29.24: Then he abandoned the gods and swiftly rushed at Śakra alone, and mighty Mahendra, of great splendour, could not see the son of his enemy.
t.7.29.25: Having struck Mātali and the horses as well with excellent arrows, he, swift of hand, showered Mahendra with a rain of shafts.
t.7.29.26: Then Śakra, abandoning his chariot and dismissing Mātali, mounted Airāvata and searched for Rāvaṇi.
t.7.29.27: But that Rākṣasa, by the power of his illusion, could not be seen in the battle as he showered Mahendra of immeasurable might with a flood of arrows.
t.7.29.28: When Rāvaṇi perceived that Indra was utterly exhausted, he then bound him by his magic power and led him toward his own army.
t.7.29.29: Then, seeing great Indra carried off by force through sorcery in that battle, all the immortals cried out, "What is this?" For the one skilled in sorcery, by whom he is being led away by magic, cannot be seen.
t.7.29.30: Meanwhile, at that very moment, all the hosts of the gods, greatly enraged, rushed upon Rāvaṇa with showers of weapons.
t.7.29.31: But Rāvaṇa, having encountered the hosts of the Vasus, Ādityas and Maruts, and being sorely afflicted by their weapons, could neither stand his ground in battle nor fight.
t.7.29.32: Seeing him, his father, exhausted in battle, his skin torn by blows, Rāvaṇi, standing invisible, spoke these words.
t.7.29.34: For this is Śakra, the lord of the army of the gods and of the three worlds; he has been seized by me, and the gods have been made to have their pride broken.
t.7.29.33: Come, father, let us two go; that work of battle is over. The victory is yours, let it be known; be at ease, free from your distress.
t.7.29.35: Having subdued your enemy by your might, enjoy the three worlds as you please. Why should you exert yourself in vain? For further battle is now fruitless for you.
t.7.29.37: Then the lord of the night-wanderers, his fever of battle gone, having won victory, went joyfully toward his palace; and on reaching his own son, he spoke these words.
t.7.29.36: He withdrew from that army of the gods and from the work of battle. Having heard those words of Rāvaṇi, Daśānana was at ease in his mind.
t.7.29.38: By those feats of valour befitting one of surpassing strength, the honour of my family has been increased, since by you, O you whose prowess equals that of the immortals, the lord of the thirty gods and the thirty gods themselves have been conquered.
t.7.29.39: Quickly lead Vāsava away to the city; go from here surrounded by the army. I too, with my ministers, will swiftly follow behind you as you go.
t.7.29.40: Then Rāvaṇi, surrounded by his army and accompanied by his mounts, having seized the lord of the thirty gods, went to his own palace; and that rākṣasa, his mind delighted, dismissed the rākṣasas.
